messages:
sre-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: high p95 latency on hosted inference (us-west1). Alert fired at 2026-03-15T02:05Z. Affected route: /v1/generate.

Alex M: I'm on call, picking this up. Initial check: many requests are p50 ~120ms, p95 ~1.8s. Customer-facing errors are low but tail latency is affecting interactive apps.

Priya R: Noted. Which clusters are impacted?

Alex M: us-west1-gpu-pool-3 primarily. CPU and GPU utilization look normal. Degraded p95 across all model types there (small models too).

Marta K: can you paste the alert graph? Any config changes in last 24h?

Alex M: putting relevant graphs and snippets here.

Alex M: ```
# p50/p95 snapshot (rolling 5m)
2026-03-15T01:58Z p50=110ms p95=300ms
2026-03-15T02:02Z p50=125ms p95=1.2s
2026-03-15T02:05Z p50=118ms p95=1.8s
2026-03-15T02:07Z p50=122ms p95=2.0s
```

Devon S: no infra deploys in the last 6h in us-west1. I do see a kernel security patch rolled to a subset of nodes at 01:50Z (linux-5.19.x -> linux-5.19.18) via autoupdate group gw-usw1-1.

Samir V: interesting — we recently saw kernel upgrades cause large tail latencies on other fleets due to changed scheduling heuristics. Any overlap with impacted hosts?

Alex M: correlating hosts now. Trace sampling coming in.

Alex M: pasted a representative trace (truncated):
```
span: request.receive 0.002ms
span: handler.dispatch 1.1ms
span: model.kv_cache.lookup 12.4ms
span: attention.kernel_dispatch 8.2ms
span: wait.cpu-sched 1080ms  <-- big
span: model.token_emit 2.7ms
```

Priya R: That `wait.cpu-sched` spike screams scheduling preemption or throttling. Does `dmesg` show anything?

Alex M: grabbed dmesg from one host: ``[02:00:59] INFO: task lwp/1234 blocked for 1200ms, sched_latency=1187ms``

Marta K: Can you run `uname -a` and `cat /sys/module/sched/parameters` on the host? Also perf counters for context-switches and scheduler migrations.

Alex M: returning outputs: ``uname -a: Linux node-32 5.19.18 #1 SMP ...`` and ``/proc/stat` snippet shows context switches jumped from ~1.2e6 to ~2.0e6 between 01:50-02:05Z.``

Devon S: that matches kernel update delta. Prior node set with 5.19.12 had stable context switch rate. Newer builds changed CFS tunables default for rcu and wakeup granularity.

Samir V: For mitigation, can we pin routing away from gw-usw1-1 group or drain updated nodes to a hot standby?

Alex M: I pushed a temporary route policy to avoid gw-usw1-1 at 02:12Z. p95 dropped to ~320ms in 2m. Rolling mitigation seemed effective.

Priya R: Good. Customer impact: only a few high-traffic customers experienced slow responses for ~12m window, support ticket triage started.

Marta K: Creating incident page for postmortem. We'll need precise timeline, affected customers, and kernel change rollouts IDs. Tagging infra for rollback decision.

Devon S: infra:autoupdate — can you halt kernel rollout to remaining nodes and prepare rollback image for gw-usw1-1? Also share kconfig diff if possible.

engbot: Action logged: incident-2026-03-15-2950001111 created. Runbook step: follow "latency-tail-kernel" playbook.

Alex M: Putting a short timeline here for the RCA thread:
- 01:50Z: kernel autoupdate started to subset (gw-usw1-1)
- 01:58Z: first small p95 bump observed
- 02:02Z: p95 climbs >1s, traces show wait.cpu-sched spans increasing
- 02:05Z: alert fired, paging sent
- 02:12Z: route policy updated to avoid gw-usw1-1
- 02:14Z: p95 returned toward baseline (~300ms)

Samir V: Hypotheses to track in-thread: [A] kernel scheduling change introduces head-of-line blocking during wakeups; [B] new kernel has a bug in rq->nr_running accounting leading to pathological preemption; [C] user-space change coincidentally aligned (low likelihood, no deploys).

Priya R: How reproducible? Can we repro on a test node by applying 5.19.18?

Devon S: I can repro in staging — I'll schedule a canary test with the exact autoupdate image. Will run perf stat with `context-switches` and `sched:sched_wakeup` histograms.

Alex M: I'm collecting traces and logs into the incident folder: <https://redwood.internal/incident/2950001111/attachments> — includes spans, dmesg, perf counters, and node lists.

Marta K: For the RCA doc we'll need: scope, timeline, mitigations, root cause analysis, and action items (rollback plan, gating autoupdate, add scheduling regression test).

Samir V: immediate action items from here:
- rollback kernel on gw-usw1-1 (infra)
- add a canary that runs our inference tail workload and watches p95 after kernel upgrades (dev-ex)
- add alert for sudden context-switch rate deltas (sre)

Alex M: handoff to morning on-call for follow-up (cc @Priya R). I'm marking this thread as stable for now; legacy nodes still being monitored.

Priya R: Acknowledged. I'll take lead on RCA write-up and coordinate with infra for rollback during maintenance window.

sre-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident status changed to: mitigated. Mitigation: routing policy applied to avoid updated nodes.

Marta K: Thanks everyone. Please append notes to the incident doc with any further traces or perf outputs. We'll do a postmortem meeting tomorrow 10:00 PST.

Alex M: TL;DR: Tail latency spike caused by kernel upgrade on subset of GPU serving hosts; route-level mitigation restored SLOs. RCA in progress.
